items.title: Supershelf
items.text:
Supershelf loads one or more profile files, walks their input directories, matches each kept file to a kind, and prints the variables for that file.

A profile is a TOML or YAML file. It names the folders to read, the rules that classify files, and the values to attach to each match. scan vars can also keep a kind file, one row per matched path. record run stores matched files in the profile database. This version does not write an output tree or a cache file.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Supershelf needs Python 3.13 or newer. From a checkout of this repository:

pip install .

supershelf --version

items.title: One profile
items.text:
Create profile.books.toml or profile.books.yaml in the directory where you will run the command. This example keeps every file under inbox and gives each one the kind unsorted.

# profile.books.toml
[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"

[[match_rules]]
name = "unsorted"
glob = "**"

# profile.books.yaml
inputs:
  - path: inbox

match_rules:
  - name: unsorted
    glob: "**"

Put a file in inbox, then list what the profile loaded and what the walk kept:

supershelf profiles
supershelf scan files

profiles prints the profile name, the file type, and the config path. scan files prints each kept file. The path column is relative to inbox.

scan kinds prints the kind for each matched file. scan vars prints the variables, and may create or append a kind file. schema prints a JSON Schema of the variables the profile declares. The documentation site has the quickstart, the guides, and the reference. From this repository, task docs serves that site.

items.title: Development
items.text: Python, uv, and task come from mise.toml. From the repository root, task test runs the tests, task docs serves the documentation, and task ci runs the tests and the docs build. GitHub Actions runs those tasks through mise. CI runs on a pull request and on a push to main, dev, or dev-*. The site publishes after that succeeds on main. test, docs:build, and docs:release can also be run on their own from the Actions tab.

items.title: Our pledge
items.text: We want this project to be a friendly and professional place for everyone who reports a bug, suggests a change, or contributes code.

items.title: Expected behavior
items.text:
• Be respectful and constructive.
  • Keep discussion on the work.
  • Use English for issues, discussions, and documentation.

  • Publishing someone else's private information.

items.title: Development
items.text:
Python, uv, and task come from mise.toml. Python is pinned to 3.13.14. The package needs Python 3.13 or newer.

Package metadata, the supershelf script, and dependencies are in pyproject.toml. The lockfile is uv.lock. Dev dependencies include pytest. Documentation dependencies are in the docs group.

From the repository root, task test runs pytest, task docs serves this site, task docs:build writes docs/site, and task ci runs the tests and that build. task docs:release publishes the site when GITHUB_OWNER is set in .env or the environment. An empty GITHUB_OWNER stops the release before the build. From docs/, the same commands are task serve, task build, and task release.

GitHub Actions installs the tools from mise.toml, then calls task. Each workflow has its own Run workflow button:

  • ci (.github/workflows/ci.yml): mise x -- task test and mise x -- task docs:build, on a pull request, on a push to main, dev, or dev-*, and on dispatch. After both succeed, a push to main also runs mise x -- task docs:release.
  • test (.github/workflows/test.yml): mise x -- task test, on dispatch only
  • docs:build (.github/workflows/docs.yml): mise x -- task docs:build, on dispatch only
  • docs:release (.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml): mise x -- task docs:release, on dispatch only. The branch you pick in that dialog is the one that is published.

  • README.md: repository overview, included as the documentation home page
  • CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md: project conduct
  • src/supershelf: the package

items.title: Concepts
items.text:
These pages state how Supershelf behaves.

flowchart LR
  discover[Discover profiles] --> walk[Walk inputs]
  walk --> match[First matching rule]
  match --> facts[File facts]
  facts --> defaults[default_vars]
  defaults --> ruleVars[Rule vars]
  ruleVars --> kindFile[Kind file row]

items.title: Errors
items.text:
User errors stop the command and print a message without a traceback. When the error includes a tip, the tip is printed too.

SupershelfError covers discovery, profile files, inputs, and match rules. A missing config, an unknown profile, a bad regex, and a path that is not a directory are this kind of error.

VarConfigError is a SupershelfError for a var table, a vars_schema entry, a kind_schema entry, a template, a module, or a kind file that is invalid as written. It exits with status 2. These are checked before the walk, except a kind file, which is checked the first time that kind and input need it. A non-template literal that cannot cast to the name's type is this error, including when a later candidate might have worked. supershelf schema uses the same check. A profile with neither vars_schema nor kind_schema stops that command with this error.

RecordConfigError is a bad record_identity word or list. It exits with status 2. The steps in this version are path and hash. A different case, an empty string, an empty list, an empty comma item, a repeated step, a template, or the word key is this error. The message names --record-identity, SUPERSHELF_RECORD_IDENTITY, config.record_identity, or the match rule (Profile NAME match rule RULE). record status and record run check every rule before the walk. Scan commands do not.

DatabaseError is a profile sqlite file that cannot be used: the parent is not a directory, the path is not a supershelf database, or the file is locked. A read accepts schema 1 and schema 2. A write migrates schema 1 to schema 2. Any other schema version is rejected. It exits with status 1. The tip names a path change or a retry.

VarResolveError is a fact or kind-file cell that cannot cast, or a mandatory name that is still unset after the last layer. A candidate list that misses does not raise it. The message names the profile, the input, the path, and the variable. The tip is the cast message for a failed fact or cell, {name} is mandatory and no layer set it. when a mandatory name is still unset, or the date-format message for a kind-file __date__ cell. There is no next candidate.

VarCandidateError is not an exit by itself. Built-in commands and user modules raise it to skip one candidate. A rendered value that misses the name's type or its validation skips that candidate the same way. The next candidate then runs. Any other exception from a module is not caught here. The command stops and the traceback is printed.

items.title: Warnings
items.text:
These do not fail the command:

  • a kept file that no rule claims
  • a missing input directory
  • an unreadable file or directory
  • a symlink cycle
  • config.profile ignored because the filename already named the profile
  • a later config format ignored because toml, yaml, or yml already won
  • a second file ignored because that profile name was already loaded
  • a duplicated path in a kind file; the first row is kept

scan inspect writes its trace to stdout. A path that no kept file has is an error for every scan command.

items.title: Inputs
items.text:
inputs is a top-level list. A missing list or a YAML null stops a scan with the "no inputs" error. inputs: [] stops with "inputs is empty". A value that is not a list also stops. supershelf profiles does not check this.

Each item is a mapping. Unknown keys stop the command. The fields are path, include, exclude, depth, and follow_symlinks.

items.title: The path
items.text:
path is required and uses the path template language. A relative path is resolved from __root_dir__.

If the path exists and is not a directory, the command stops. If the directory is missing, Supershelf logs a warning and skips that input. The input keeps its 1-based position, so a later input is still index 2 when the first was skipped. The skipped input adds no rows.

items.title: Depth, symlinks, and globs
items.text:
depth defaults to 0. 0 means no recursion limit. 1 means only the input directory. 2 means that directory and one subdirectory level. A negative depth stops the command.

follow_symlinks defaults to true. false skips symlinks. A followed symlink is stored as the path under the input, not as the target path. A symlink cycle logs a warning and that path is skipped.

include and exclude are lists of globs. They match the path relative to the input directory. * stays in one directory. ** crosses directories. The match is against the whole relative path.

If include is set, a file must match at least one include pattern. If include is omitted or null, the walk starts from every file it found. include: [] keeps no file. If exclude is set, matching files are dropped. If exclude is omitted, null, or [], nothing is dropped for that reason. Exclude runs after include.

**/*.pdf matches a PDF in any nested directory. *.pdf matches a PDF sitting in the input directory only.

items.title: What is kept
items.text:
The walk keeps regular files that pass include and exclude. Within one input, paths are sorted.

Skipped, and not recorded:

  • directories, which are entered only while depth allows
  • symlinks when follow_symlinks is false
  • symlink cycles
  • empty files
  • anything that is not a regular file
  • files that fail include or match exclude

An unreadable file or directory logs a warning and is skipped. That directory is not descended.

scan files then reads mtime, ctime, and sha256, unless --quick is set. An unreadable file at that step logs a warning and is dropped. --quick still ignores empty files. It does not hash.

Stored mtime and ctime are UTC ISO-8601 with a numeric offset, so they can be parsed later. Fractional seconds are included when the filesystem value has them. scan files shows those instants with config.default_date_format.

path in the table is relative to the input directory, with / separators. input is the 1-based index in that profile's inputs list.

scan files takes an optional path, the same text as that column. Omit it to list every kept file. If any kept path equals the selector, every input lists that exact path only. Otherwise the selector lists paths that start with it. A value that no kept file has stops the command. The same path in two inputs is listed twice.

The columns are profile, input, path, mtime, ctime, and sha256. --quick omits the last three.

scan files only prints. It does not create the database file or the cache file.

items.title: Kind files
items.text:
A kind file stores one row per path for one kind. scan vars reads that row after the winning rule's vars. This is the last assignment layer. Each cell is one literal string, then cast to the name's type. It replaces a value the rule already stored. It does not change what the rule template already read. A cell that cannot cast stops the file. It has no next candidate.

scan files and scan kinds do not read or write kind files. The file shape is in Kind file.

items.title: Which file
items.text:
config.kind_overrides_config is an optional list of path templates. They use the path template language. Omitted, the list is:

{{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.{{ __kind__ }}.csv
{{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.{{ __kind__ }}.toml
{{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.{{ __kind__ }}.yaml
{{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.{{ __kind__ }}.yml

An empty list means no kind files. Nothing is created or appended.

Each path is rendered with the profile scope, __kind__ set to the rule kind, and __input__.path set to the absolute input directory. A relative result is resolved from __root_dir__. The first path that exists and is a file wins. A missing path tries the next. None found means no row, unless the mode is always. A path that exists and is not a file stops the command. A symlink to a file is that file. A bad suffix, or content that does not parse, stops the command. The next path is not tried.

The rule kind picks the file.

The row key is the path relative to the input, with / separators. It is an exact match. Case is not folded. Two inputs that share one kind file treat the same relative path as one row. Put {{ __input__.path }} in a template when those inputs must not share rows.

The parsed file is cached on that profile by its absolute path. Another profile in the same command does not share the cache. The winner is cached by kind and input directory. Nothing is written to cache_file. A kind with no matched file is never looked up, so always does not create a file for it.

-vv logs each path tried the first time a kind and input directory are searched: a missing path, the file when it is first loaded, or a path already loaded for another search. The search stops at the first existing file, so later templates are not rendered and are not logged. An empty list logs that there is no candidate list, except when the mode is disabled. A repeated search stays quiet. -v does not add these lines. disabled does not search.

items.title: Mode
items.text:
config.kind_overrides_mode is auto, manual, always, or disabled. Omitted means auto. The words are exact. Any other value stops the command.

--kind-overrides-mode belongs to scan vars. SUPERSHELF_KIND_OVERRIDES_MODE accepts the same four words. The flag wins over the environment variable. The environment variable wins over the config key. Unset means omitted. A different case, or an empty environment value, is an error.

Mode Existing file No file found auto Read it. Append matched paths that have no row. No row, and no new file. manual Read it. Leave it unchanged. No row. always Read it. Append matched paths that have no row. Create the first template, then append those paths. disabled Ignore it. No row. The path list is not rendered.

An empty file, or a file of whitespace only, is an empty table. auto and always replace it with a new file. manual leaves those bytes unchanged.

always creates missing parent directories. If a parent exists and is a file, that is an error and no kind file is written.

auto and always do not delete a row, edit a cell, drop a column, or reorder rows. They do not rewrite existing cell text. When schema columns are missing from a CSV, those names are appended on the right and existing rows gain empty cells. A path already present is not appended again, including a duplicate row that was warned and kept as the first. New rows follow the walk, input index first. A new row sets PATH in CSV, or path in TOML and YAML. The other cells are empty, so a row created on this run does not change this run's values.

A non-empty file whose last byte is not a newline gets a newline, then the new rows. The new bytes are one write at the end. A crash during that write can leave a partial last row. There is no lock. Two overlapping runs can append the same path twice.

Writes happen after the run succeeds. A variable error writes nothing.

--dry-run reads when the mode reads, and does not create, append, or add columns. It logs only when something would change. A file that would be created logs its path and its row count. A file that would gain rows logs its path and how many rows would be appended. A CSV that would gain schema columns logs those names, even when no row would be appended. Otherwise zero rows logs nothing. manual and disabled log nothing. Those lines are info logs, so -v shows them.

When scan vars is given a path, only the selected files are matched, so only those paths can be appended.

items.title: Cells
items.text:
A cell is one stored string. It is not a candidate list, and it is not compiled as Jinja, even when the text contains {{, {%, or {#. An empty cell, a blank string, or a YAML or TOML null is absent. The previous layer stays. There is no way to force an empty string over a previous value. Surrounding spaces are kept, except on __date__.

A cell that sets an existing key keeps that key's first position and replaces the stored string. A new key is appended. CSV uses column order. TOML and YAML use key order inside vars.

A row must not set an internal name. __date__ is allowed. __kind__ stays the kind from the match rule.

Unmatched files have no kind, so they get no row. Files the walk skipped get no row.

items.title: Document date
items.text:
A kind-file __date__ cell is parsed. The format is config.kind_overrides_date_format. When that key is omitted or null, the format is config.default_date_format, which defaults to %Y-%m-%d. The format is checked before the walk. It must be a non-empty string, valid for strptime, and it must include a year, a month, and a day. A time portion is allowed.

The cell is stripped, then the whole string is parsed. The stored value is YYYY-MM-DD. A parsed time is dropped. A value that does not match stops the command. The message names the file, the profile, the input, the path, the cell text, and the format. There is no next candidate. A blank __date__ cell is absent, and the command does not stop.

This format applies to __date__ only. In TOML and YAML, another key, including date, stays raw text.

config.kind_overrides_sep is checked before the walk, at the same time as the date format. The separator rules are in Kind file.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
This version records matched files. It does not build an output tree.

  • There is no output tree. outputs is not read. extension_remap is not read.
  • record run creates database_file when a row would change. scan vars and record run create it when meta() runs and the cache misses. --dry-run does not. scan files and scan kinds do not. scan inspect, schema, and profiles do not create it either. cache_file is rendered and nothing writes it. See Record.
  • scan vars may create or append a kind file, and may add missing schema columns to a CSV. It does not edit a cell that is already there. scan files and scan kinds do not read or write kind files. See Kind files.
  • supershelf schema prints JSON Schema for vars_schema and kind_schema. It does not walk inputs or write a kind file. Kind-file columns are chosen when scan vars writes a CSV. With no schema columns, a new CSV still starts as PATH,__date__.
  • --dry-run on scan vars still reads kind files and does not create or append. The other scan commands only print. schema only prints. --dry-run on record run prints the rows that would change and creates nothing.
  • pdf_cdate() and pdf_mdate() read PDF creation and modification dates. meta() reads more fields from the file, including PDF info, exiftool tags, and pdftotext. There is no scan meta command.

A __date__ value is stored for later output paths. Nothing in this version writes a path from it.

items.title: Matching
items.text:
match_rules is a profile-level list, a sibling of inputs. Every input of that profile uses it. Patterns are literal. They are not templates.

scan kinds uses the files scan files would keep, without hashing and without reading mtime or ctime. It prints matched files only. Columns: profile, input, path, kind, rule. input and path mean the same thing as in scan files. It takes the same optional path, and it matches and warns only for the selected files.

items.title: First hit wins
items.text:
For each kept file, rules are tried in list order. The first rule that matches wins. Later rules are not tried.

A rule matches when one field matches. Fields are tried in this order. The first hit wins. Later fields are not tried.

  1. regex
  2. directory_regex
  3. filename_regex
  4. glob
  5. directory_glob
  6. filename_glob

A field may be a string or a list of strings. A string is one pattern. Patterns in a list are tried in order. The first hit wins. An omitted field or an empty list is skipped.

For input directory /srv/in and file /srv/in/Bank2000/card/statement.pdf:

  • regex and glob see Bank2000/card/statement.pdf, the path relative to the input, with / separators.
  • directory_regex and directory_glob see Bank2000/card. That is the path between the input directory and the file, with no filename and no leading or trailing slash.
  • filename_regex and filename_glob see statement.pdf.
  • A file in the input directory has an empty directory. directory_regex and directory_glob do not match it.
  • The input directory is that input's path, not config.root_dir.
  • A symlink uses the path stored under the input.

items.title: Regex and glob
items.text:
Regex is anchored to the whole candidate. The engine full-matches. Authors do not write ^ or $. A pattern that stops before the extension does not match a file that has one. directory_regex has no filename, so it does not include an extension.

Globs full-match the whole candidate, with the same * and ** rules as include and exclude. ** also matches a file sitting in the input directory, so glob = "**" claims every kept file. A glob does not capture groups. * consumes the extension, so filename_glob = "REL*" matches REL_1.pdf.

Named groups from the winning regex are kept. Unnamed groups are ignored. Groups are not merged across fields or rules. A group name that starts with __ is a config error, checked before the walk. A group whose name repeats an internal fact is dropped, because those facts are already set.

Patterns are compiled once per profile, before the walk. A bad pattern stops the command before that walk.

items.title: Name and kind
items.text:
A rule needs a name, a kind, or both. A blank value counts as omitted.

  • When both are set, the kind is the explicit kind and the rule name stays name.
  • When only name is set, the kind is that name.
  • When only kind is set, the rule name is that kind.

The rule name must be unique in the profile. A duplicate stops the command. Several rules may share one kind when their names differ. A rule with neither name nor kind, or with no patterns, stops the command.

Unknown keys on a rule are ignored while matching. vars is read later by scan vars, from the raw rule mapping.

If match_rules is missing, or a file matches no rule:

  • A warning names the profile, the input, and the relative path.
  • The file stays on the scan result, with the data the walk already gathered.
  • It is left out of the matched set. No kind is stored.
  • scan kinds does not show that file.
  • Warnings do not fail the command.

Files the walk skipped never reach matching. scan kinds does not create the database file or the cache file.

items.title: Modules
items.text:
config.var_modules is an optional list of importable module paths. Omitted or empty means no user modules.

Built-in commands are always registered first. Then each module is imported in list order, before the walk. An import failure stops the command.

A module may export two mappings:

  • GLOBALS: call them as {{ name(...) }}
  • FILTERS: call them as {{ value | name(...) }}

Values are callables. They should accept strings and return a string. A return value that is not a string fails that candidate. Raising VarCandidateError fails that candidate and lets the next one run. Any other exception stops the command.

A name that repeats a built-in command, a Jinja name, or an earlier module, stops the command. Built-in commands cannot be replaced. Keys must be strings. A mapping that is not a mapping, or a value that is not callable, stops the command.

my_package/supershelf_vars.py
from supershelf.errors import VarCandidateError


def account_tail(value: str) -> str:
    if len(value) < 4:
        raise VarCandidateError("account is too short")
    return value[-4:]


GLOBALS = {"account_tail": account_tail}
TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[config]
var_modules = ["my_package.supershelf_vars"]
profile.books.yaml
config:
  var_modules:
    - my_package.supershelf_vars

{{ account_tail(account) }}

FILTERS may be omitted. GLOBALS may be omitted. A module that exports neither adds no commands.

items.title: Paths
items.text:
Profile paths use a small template language. Variable values use Jinja, which is a different language. Both are compared in Templates.

A path template replaces {{ name }} and {{ name.key }} once. Spaces inside the braces are allowed. The name must already be in scope. Dotted keys read nested mappings. The value must be a string. Text taken from the scope is not rendered again, so a value that itself contains {{ is stored as text.

Unknown names, missing keys, and non-string values stop the command. There are no filters and no function calls.

items.title: Render order
items.text:
These config keys are rendered in order. After each one, a relative result is resolved from the directory that contains the config file, stored as an absolute path, and published in the scope before the next key renders.

Key Scope name Default root_dir __root_dir__ {{ __profile_dir__ }} database_file __database_file__ {{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.sqlite cache_file __cache_file__ {{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.cache

~ is expanded. An empty result stops the command. A relative database_file such as state.sqlite is resolved from the config directory, not from root_dir. To place it under the root, write {{ __root_dir__ }}/state.sqlite.

config.default_date_format is a plain string. It is not a template. The default is %Y-%m-%d. It formats mtime and ctime in scan files. The stored timestamps used by variables stay UTC ISO-8601.

scan vars and record run create database_file when meta() runs and the cache misses. --dry-run does not. scan files and scan kinds do not. record run also creates database_file when a row would change. Nothing writes cache_file. The paths are rendered so later templates can read them.

items.title: Other paths
items.text:
inputs.path uses this same language, with the profile scope. A relative result is resolved from __root_dir__.

kind_overrides_config uses it too. For that render, the scope also has __kind__ and __input__.path. __input__.path is the absolute input directory. A relative result is resolved from __root_dir__. Those two names are not part of the general profile scope, so an input path cannot read them.

The names available in the profile scope are listed in Variable names.

items.title: Profiles
items.text:
A profile is one config file. Supershelf loads a list of them, then a command can filter that list. supershelf profiles prints profile, type, and path. It does not render path templates and does not scan inputs.

The file must be a mapping. TOML and YAML are accepted. The stored type is toml or yaml. A .yml file is stored as yaml.

items.title: Where files come from
items.text:
The first source that yields a file wins. Later sources are not merged in.

  1. --config points at a file or a directory. It overrides SUPERSHELF_CONFIG. A missing path, or a directory with no matching file, stops the command. Supershelf does not fall through to the current directory.
  2. SUPERSHELF_CONFIG, when it is set to a non-blank value, uses the same path rules as --config. A blank or whitespace value is unset, and discovery continues. A blank or whitespace --config stops the command.
  3. The current directory.
  4. The user config directory: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/supershelf, or ~/.config/supershelf when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset or empty.

An explicit file is loaded as that file only. An explicit directory uses the directory rules below.

In the current directory, and in an explicit directory, a singleton wins. If supershelf.toml, supershelf.yaml, or supershelf.yml exists, Supershelf loads only the first of those, in that order. It does not also load profile.NAME.* from that directory. A later format is ignored, with a warning.

If there is no singleton, Supershelf loads every:

  • profile.NAME.toml
  • profile.NAME.yaml
  • profile.NAME.yml

One file per name. Preference is toml, then yaml, then yml. A later format is ignored, with a warning. Names are sorted.

The user config directory does not treat supershelf.toml as a profile source. Only profile.NAME.* files are loaded there.

If none of these sources has a file, the command stops.

items.title: The profile name
items.text:
When the filename is profile.NAME.*, the profile name is NAME. If config.profile is a different non-empty string, it is ignored and a warning is printed. The same name does not warn. A blank config.profile is unset.

When the filename has no profile.NAME prefix, the name is config.profile when that is a non-empty string, otherwise default. A file passed with --config follows this same rule.

The stored document always has config.profile set to the resolved name.

If two loaded files resolve to the same name, the later file is ignored, with a warning. The first is kept.

items.title: Which profiles a command uses
items.text:
Selection happens after the files are loaded.

  • --profile wins over SUPERSHELF_PROFILES.
  • Both accept a comma-separated list. Spaces around names are ignored.
  • A blank --profile stops the command. A blank or whitespace SUPERSHELF_PROFILES is unset.
  • The result keeps the requested order. A repeated name is kept once.
  • An unknown name stops the command. The message lists the known names.
  • With no selector, every discovered profile is kept.

Each selected profile is scanned on its own. Profiles do not share results.

items.title: Record
items.text:
record stores each matched file in the profile sqlite file. The path is config.database_file. The packaged path is {{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.sqlite. One profile has one file. cache_file is a different path, and nothing writes it.

scan vars and record run create the sqlite file when meta() runs and the cache misses. --dry-run does not. scan files and scan kinds do not. scan inspect, schema, and profiles do not either. record run also creates it when a row would change. --dry-run prints those rows and creates nothing.

The walk is the same full walk as scan vars. Variables are resolved the same way, including a kind-file read. record does not create or append a kind file.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
PATH is the same selector as scan files. On record status and record run, a value that matches no kept file and no recorded document stops the command.

Command What it prints Write record status [PATH] Every in-scope matched file, plus a document this scan would mark missing or unmatched No record run [PATH] The same rows, except unchanged Yes, unless --dry-run record history [PATH] Events, oldest first No record duplicates [PATH] Hashes carried by two or more documents No

record history and record duplicates do not scan. With no database they print no rows. A history path matches a document when any of its event paths, or its current path, equals the selector or starts with it. The command then prints every event for that document, so a move is still found from the old path.

Status words:

Status Meaning new First time this document is recorded. Generation 1. generation New bytes at the document's path. The previous generation stays in the history. move The same hash is at a new path and the old path is gone. The generation number stays. vars Kind, rule, or variables changed. The generation number stays. missing The path left the walked inputs. The row stays. present A missing or unmatched document matched again, with the same hash and variables. unmatched The file is still in the walk, and no rule matches. The last hash and variables stay. refresh Only mtime, ctime, or the input index changed. No history row. unchanged Nothing to write. record run leaves this row out. duplicate An extra live file whose hash this run already keeps. It is printed and not inserted.

duplicates on a status row counts other present documents with that hash, including documents outside the path filter, plus other extra files reported as duplicate for that hash. record duplicates is the wider query: a hash is listed when two or more documents have carried it, including an older generation. current is yes when that hash is the document's hash now. A file that was never inserted does not appear there.

items.title: What stays the same document
items.text:
A document has a stable id. Rows are not deleted. A later revert walks the events.

The location is the input directory plus the path relative to that input. Reordering the inputs list is not a move. A missing input directory leaves that input's documents as they are.

record_identity chooses the link when a scan could be read two ways. The packaged default is path. For the profile default, --record-identity wins, then SUPERSHELF_RECORD_IDENTITY, then config.record_identity. A match rule's record_identity wins over that default for files that rule claims. Omitted or null on the rule inherits the profile default. The flag does not override a rule that set the key.

A bare word expands. path means path then hash. hash means hash then path. A list does not expand: [path] is the path step only, and [hash] is the hash step only. The flag and the environment variable are a word or a comma-separated list (hash, path). The profile value and the rule value are a string or a list of strings.

The list is tried in order. The first step that matches links the document. events.identity stores the first step of that list, path or hash, even when a later step did the work. meta.identity stores the profile default only, as path,hash or hash,path. A stored path compares equal to path,hash. A stored hash compares equal to hash,path. A rule override is not written to meta.

path. A file that is still at the recorded path keeps that document. New bytes there are a new generation. A move happens when the recorded path is gone, exactly one in-scope file has the hash, and only one document wants that hash.

hash. The current hash owns the document among hash-first files. One live file with that hash is that document, including when the old path now holds different bytes. Those new bytes are a new document. A second hash-first file with that hash is duplicate and is not inserted. On a first run the lower path is the new document.

Both rules agree when a file is renamed and edited in the same run. The old path is gone and the old hash is not live, so the old document becomes missing and the new path is a new document.

Changing the profile default warns once and still updates meta when no document row changes. Changing one rule's list warns once for that rule name. --dry-run warns too. Old events keep the identity word that wrote them. path and [path, hash] are the same list, so that change does not warn. A bad list, a template, or the word key stops record status and record run before the walk. Scan commands ignore the key.

A path filter observes only the selected paths. It does not mark, move, or insert anything outside that set. A filtered run can mark a selected path missing while those bytes still exist under another name. A later run with no path can move the document onto that name.

Bank2000 invoice 2026-04-25.pdf is recorded. The next scan finds new bytes at that path, and the old bytes at 2026-04-25-copy.pdf.

With path, 2026-04-25.pdf stays the same document and gains a generation. 2026-04-25-copy.pdf is a second document. record duplicates lists the old hash on both. The first document's row says current no.

With hash, the old hash moves to 2026-04-25-copy.pdf. The new bytes at 2026-04-25.pdf are a new document.

items.title: History and a later output
items.text:
Each change appends an event: new, move, generation, vars, missing, present, or unmatched. A refresh does not. Deleting an event is not how a revert works.

The event row also has room for a later output apply: output name, operation (copy, symlink, or hardlink), destination, source hash, and the previous state of that destination. No command writes that event yet. This version does not build an output tree.

items.title: Template commands
items.text:
Variable templates can call these commands. They are registered on every profile. A user module cannot replace these names. See Modules.

A miss raises VarCandidateError. That fails the current candidate only, so the next string in the list can run. The call needs parentheses. pdf_cdate without () is the command object, not the date.

items.title: regex_time_var
items.text:
regex_time_var(value, format, ...) reads a string and tries each strptime format. The first hit wins. The result is YYYY-MM-DD. At least one format is required. Formats are separate arguments, because a format such as %H:%M:%S contains colons.

{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y%m%d") }}

date is the variable of that name, often a regex group. The command does not read __date__ unless you pass that name. A value that matches no format fails the candidate.

items.title: regex_replace
items.text:
regex_replace(value, pattern, replacement) substitutes on that string. Three strings are required. Backreferences are allowed. No match fails the candidate. An invalid pattern fails the candidate.

{{ regex_replace(account, "[0-9]{4}$", "") }}

items.title: file
items.text: file("ctime") and file("mtime") return the same UTC ISO-8601 timestamps as __ctime__ and __mtime__. Any other argument fails the candidate. The result includes the time. It is not rewritten to YYYY-MM-DD, so it does not satisfy __date__ by itself.

items.title: pdf_cdate and pdf_mdate
items.text:
pdf_cdate() and pdf_mdate() read the PDF creation and modification dates. The result is YYYY-MM-DD. A file that is not a PDF, a missing date, or an unreadable file fails the candidate.

The file is opened only when a candidate calls one of these. Both dates for one file hash are read once for that profile. Another profile in the same command reads the file again. A failed read is cached too, so a later candidate in that profile does not open the file again.

meta() reads other fields from the file. See Limits.

items.title: meta
items.text:
meta(driver, field) returns one metadata field. field may be omitted only for a driver whose only result is text, such as pdftotext.

{{ meta("fs", "name") }}
{{ meta("pdf", "author") }}
{{ meta("pdftotext") }}

A disabled driver, a file the driver does not accept, a missing field, or a tool failure fails that candidate. The next string in the list can run. pdf_cdate() and pdf_mdate() do not use this cache.

items.title: Variables
items.text:
scan vars takes the kept files, then the matched set, and prints one row per matched file. Columns: profile, input, path, kind, rule, vars, sources.

kind is __kind__ from the match rule. rule stays the match rule name. vars is one cell. Each set variable is one line: the name, :, then the display string. Names are sorted alphabetically. An unset variable is left out. sources is the next column. It has one line per name, in that same order. Each line is the labels that wrote the name, joined by ,. csv uses those same two cells. --format json and --format yaml omit the sources column. They replace vars with one object per name: value is the Python value, and value_sources is the label list. display is not in the object. A float can have value 12.5 while the table shows 12.50. date, time, and datetime use the accepted spelling for both value and the table.

Source labels are fact, default, rule:<rule name>, and kind:<kind file path>. A later write appends a label. It keeps the earlier ones. The last label is the winner. A layer that misses does not add a label and does not remove earlier ones.

Internal names are left out of vars and sources, and out of the json and yaml objects, unless --all is set. __date__, schema names, regex groups, and other assigned names stay.

The walk is the full walk. mtime, ctime, and sha256 are required. There is no --quick. The path argument is the same as scan files: omit it to list every matched file. If any kept path equals the selector, every input lists that exact path only. Otherwise the selector lists paths that start with it. A value that no kept file has stops the command. The same path in two inputs is listed twice. When a path is set, only the selected files are matched, so other files are not warned.

Unmatched files log the same warning as scan kinds, once per file. They add no row.

scan vars and record run create the database file when meta() runs and the cache misses. --dry-run does not. scan files and scan kinds do not. This command does not create the cache file or an output tree. It may read, create, or append a kind file. See Kind files.

items.title: Facts and assignments
items.text:
Facts are the base scope. An assignment of the same name shadows that fact for later templates and replaces the printed value. While a key is being rendered, a reference to itself still sees the previous layer, so the fact stays visible when no earlier assignment set that name.

Profile scope from Paths is available to templates. It is not printed.

Internal facts stay in scope for templates. scan vars prints them only with --all:

  • __kind__: the kind from matching
  • __rule_name__: the match rule name
  • __ctime__ and __mtime__: the stored UTC ISO-8601 timestamps, not default_date_format
  • __file_hash__: lowercase sha256
  • __file_name__: the filename
  • __file_stem__: the filename without its last suffix. archive.tar.gz stores archive.tar
  • __file_ext__: the last suffix without the leading dot. archive.tar.gz stores gz. A name with no suffix stores an empty string. A leading dot, as in .gitignore, is not a suffix, so the extension is empty and the stem is the whole name
  • __file_path__: the path relative to the input, with / separators
  • __file_dir__: the directory relative to the input. Empty when the file sits in the input directory

Named groups from the winning regex are facts. They are stored in the order the pattern declared them. The table sorts every printed name alphabetically.

items.title: Layers
items.text:
Assignments are the user layers. Later wins on the same key. Each layer is applied before the next one starts.

  1. default_vars
  2. match_rules vars for the winning rule.
  3. The kind-file row for that path. See Kind files. This is the last assignment layer.

default_vars and rule vars must not set an internal name. A kind-file row must not either. __kind__ stays the kind from the match rule.

__date__ is not an internal. Any of these layers may set it. The filename does not. A stem that is a date stays __file_stem__. To use it, write a candidate such as {{ regex_time_var(__file_stem__, __default_date_format__) }}. A kind-file __date__ cell is parsed into YYYY-MM-DD. The other layers use candidates.

Omitted default_vars, omitted rule vars, or no kind-file cells for that path means that layer is empty.

A later write replaces the display string and keeps the name's earlier source labels. The kind-file row is applied after the rule template has stored its string, so the rule does not read the cell. The table sorts every printed name alphabetically, and the sources column follows that order.

items.title: Types
items.text:
vars_schema is an optional top-level mapping. Each key is a variable name. A name with no entry is text. A kind can point at those names. See Kind schema.

type is text, int, float, bool, date, time, or datetime, in lower case. date is YYYY-MM-DD. time is HH:MM or HH:MM:SS. datetime is YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, and a set value always includes a clock. No timezone and no fractional seconds. Seconds stay in the display only when they were written. 15:04 and 15:04:00 match as the same clock in allowed and in range checks. A bool accepts true, yes, and 1, or false, no, and 0, in any case. The display is true or false. An int display drops a leading + and leading zeros, so 007 prints as 7.

Built-in facts are text, except __date__, which is date. __ctime__ and __mtime__ stay text, because they include fractional seconds and a UTC offset. A user entry may set desc and unit on a locked built-in. On __date__ it may also set mandatory, default, and validation. A new name that starts with __ stops the command. internal: true on a user name stops the command.

Other keys on a user entry: desc, unit, mandatory (default false), default, and validation. Unknown keys stop the command. mandatory is checked after the last layer. None fails the file. An empty text string is set, so it passes.

default and default_vars are one slot. Setting the same name in both stops the command. A schema entry with no default takes the default_vars value. default_vars stays a string or a list of strings. vars_schema.<name>.default may also be a typed literal (12, 1.5, true). Quote date, time, and datetime defaults. null is not unset. Omit the key.

validation may set allowed. text, date, time, and datetime may also set pattern, min_length, and max_length. pattern must match the whole display string. int, float, date, time, and datetime may set ge, gt, le, and lt. A constraint that does not apply to the type stops the command.

A list in an assignment is a candidate list: the first success is kept, and the stored value is one scalar. type: list stops the command. A kind-file cell is one string, not a candidate list.

Jinja reads the display string after a successful cast. It does not receive the Python value. {{ amount + 1 }} is not integer math. regex_replace and regex_time_var still receive strings. regex_time_var returns YYYY-MM-DD, which satisfies date and misses time and datetime.

A regex group is cast when the fact is stored. A group that does not match its type stops the file. There is no next candidate. Capture the raw text under another name when a later candidate list should supply the typed value.

items.title: Kind schema
items.text:
kind_schema is an optional top-level mapping. Each key is a kind name. A file whose kind is not listed keeps the profile catalog.

A kind has desc and vars_schema. Each key under that vars_schema is a variable name for files of that kind. The value names a declared vars_schema entry, or __date__. A string is that name (my_amount: amount). Null or a blank string uses the local name. In YAML, amount: is null. TOML has no null, so write amount = "". An object may omit schema, and the local name is used (tax: {mandatory: true} uses tax). That catalog entry supplies type and internal. The kind cannot set those.

Omitted desc, unit, mandatory, and validation are copied from the catalog entry. A validation mapping on the kind replaces the catalog one. default is not copied. Set it on the kind when that local name needs a default. Profile default and default_vars apply to that catalog name on files whose kind is not listed. On a listed kind they apply only when that kind's vars_schema includes the name.

When the kind lists a name the profile also has, files of that kind use the kind's spec. mandatory: false there leaves the name optional for that kind. Names the kind does not list stay on the profile spec, including profile mandatory.

supershelf schema prints one JSON document, keyed by profile name. It does not walk inputs. With kind_schema, each kind is an object under $defs. Without it, the object is the declared vars_schema names. Locked internals are left out. __date__ is included only when vars_schema.__date__ is set. If neither key is set, the command stops with status 2. The schema describes resolved values, not the strings in a kind file or in rule vars. auto and always add missing schema columns on the right of a CSV. A name that is not a legal column is left out. With no schema columns, a new CSV still starts as PATH,__date__.

items.title: Candidates
items.text:
A var table is a mapping. This section is default_vars and rule vars. A kind-file cell is one string, then cast to the name's type. Each key matches [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. Each value is a string, or a list of strings. A string is one candidate. A list is an ordered fallback. An empty list stops the command. Numbers, booleans, nulls, dates, and nested mappings stop the command in these layers. Quote scalars such as 2026-04-25. In YAML, also quote yes, no, on, and off. Those words become booleans before Supershelf reads them, and a boolean is a config error here. Typed literals belong on vars_schema.<name>.default.

A candidate with no {{, {%, or {# is a literal string. It is not compiled. Any other candidate is a Jinja template. Each distinct template source is compiled once for that profile. Another profile in the same command compiles it again. Rendered results are not cached. A syntax error stops the command when that template is loaded. Shape errors in default_vars and rule vars are checked before the walk. A kind file is checked the first time that kind and input need it. kind_overrides_sep and kind_overrides_date_format are checked before the walk.

Jinja uses strict undefined names. autoescape is off. An unknown name fails that candidate. The rendered string is then cast to the name's type. A cast miss or a validation miss fails that candidate. The first candidate that does not fail is kept. The list is not kept. Later templates read the display string. Inserted strings are not rendered again. A non-template literal that cannot cast stops the command when the table is loaded, including when a later candidate might have worked.

A template can read facts and any assignment already rendered. It cannot read a key later in the same mapping. That name is not defined yet. The key being rendered sees the previous layer's string, not the candidate list being tried. account = "{{ account }}" reads the group when no earlier layer defined account. A default_vars value hides the group from the rule template of the same name. A rule's {{ __date__ }} reads the __date__ string the earlier layer already kept. It does not run that layer's other candidates again.

An empty string is a success for text. For int, float, bool, date, time, and datetime, empty or whitespace is a miss. __date__ is date, so an empty string misses.

If every candidate in a layer misses, that layer does not write the name. An earlier value stays. When no layer has written it, the name stays unset and is left off the row. The command continues. mandatory runs after the last layer, and None stops the file. A fact or a kind-file cell that cannot cast still stops the file. There is no next candidate for those. This version does not write output paths.

A function that has nothing to return fails that candidate only, by raising VarCandidateError. Any other exception from a template stops the command. Built-in commands are documented in Template commands.

items.title: List files
items.text: supershelf scan files prints the files one input keeps. The rules for the walk are in Inputs.

items.title: A folder of statements
items.text:
These examples use profile books, from profile.books.toml or profile.books.yaml in the quickstart. This profile reads inbox. It keeps PDF files and drops anything under a draft directory. depth 0 walks every nested directory.

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"
depth = 0
include = ["**/*.pdf"]
exclude = ["**/draft/**"]

[[match_rules]]
name = "unsorted"
glob = "**"
profile.books.yaml
inputs:
  - path: inbox
    depth: 0
    include:
      - "**/*.pdf"
    exclude:
      - "**/draft/**"

match_rules:
  - name: unsorted
    glob: "**"

path is resolved from the profile root. A relative path such as inbox starts at root_dir, which defaults to the directory of the config file. See Paths.

supershelf scan files

Example columns for one kept file:

profile  input  path                                      mtime       ctime       sha256
books    1      Bank2000/REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf        2026-04-25  2026-04-25  0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

input is the 1-based position of that input in the profile, not the folder path. path is relative to the input directory. mtime and ctime are shown with config.default_date_format, which defaults to %Y-%m-%d. sha256 is the lowercase hex digest of the file bytes.

Omit the path to list every kept file. The argument is that path column: directory and filename, relative to the input.

supershelf scan files "Bank2000/REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf"
supershelf scan files Bank2000

An exact file path lists that file only. The same path in two inputs is listed twice. If any kept path equals the selector, every input uses that exact path only, so a file named Bank2000 does not also list Bank2000.txt. Otherwise the selector lists paths that start with it, so Bank2000 lists Bank2000/card/CARD_1234_20211231.pdf and Bank2000.txt when no kept file is exactly Bank2000. A value that no kept file has stops the command.

supershelf scan files --quick

--quick prints profile, input, and path only. It does not read mtime, ctime, or the hash.

Empty files are left out. A missing input directory is a warning, and that input is skipped. A path that exists and is not a directory stops the command.

The next page classifies those files: Match a kind.

items.title: Match a kind
items.text:
supershelf scan kinds prints each kept file that a rule claims, with the rule name and the kind. Matching rules are in Matching.

Rules run in list order. The first rule that matches wins. Put specific rules first and a catch-all last.

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_statement"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = 'REL_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<receipt_id>\w{8})\.pdf'

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_card"
kind = "invoice"
directory_glob = "Bank2000/card"

[[match_rules]]
name = "unsorted"
glob = "**"
profile.books.yaml
inputs:
  - path: inbox

match_rules:
  - name: bank2000_statement
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: 'REL_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<receipt_id>\w{8})\.pdf'

  - name: bank2000_card
    kind: invoice
    directory_glob: Bank2000/card

  - name: unsorted
    glob: "**"

filename_regex is compared with the filename only, and it must match the whole name, including .pdf. directory_glob is compared with the directory under the input. For inbox/Bank2000/card/CARD_1234_20211231.pdf that directory is Bank2000/card. A file sitting directly in inbox has an empty directory, so a directory pattern does not claim it.

glob = "**" claims every remaining kept file. kind is omitted, so the kind is the rule name, unsorted.

supershelf scan kinds

Example:

profile  input  path                                         kind     rule
books    1      Bank2000/REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf           invoice  bank2000_statement
books    1      Bank2000/card/CARD_1234_20211231.pdf         invoice  bank2000_card
books    1      notes/readme.txt                             unsorted unsorted

The path argument is the same as List files. Omit it to classify every kept file. If any kept path equals the selector, every input classifies that exact path only. Otherwise the selector classifies paths that start with it.

A kept file that no rule claims is absent from this table. The command warns once for that file and still exits successfully. A path argument limits both the table and those warnings to the selected files. scan files still lists that file.

Two rules may share a kind. Rule names in one profile must be unique.

The next page shows the patterns behind one of those rows: See why it matched.

items.title: Record matched files
items.text:
record keeps a history of the files a profile matches. The concepts are in Record. This version does not build an output tree.

Use the profile from Set variables, with a file in inbox:

[default_vars]
vendor = "Bank2000"

[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"

[[match_rules]]
name = "bill"
glob = "**"

Preview the rows a run would write. This creates nothing, including the sqlite file:

supershelf record run --dry-run

The status is new. Write it:

supershelf record run

That creates profile.<name>.sqlite next to the config file, unless config.database_file says otherwise. A second run with no file changes prints no rows.

record status prints every matched file, including unchanged. record history prints the events. record duplicates prints hashes that belong to more than one document.

Rename the file and keep the bytes, then run again. The history shows move for the same document. Replace the bytes at the same path and the history shows generation. Delete the file and the document becomes missing. The row stays. record history still prints it.

scan vars and record run create the sqlite file when meta() runs and the cache misses. --dry-run does not. scan files and scan kinds do not. record reads kind files the same way scan vars does, and it does not create or append one.

To follow the hash instead of the path when both change in one run, set the link rule:

supershelf record run --record-identity hash

A comma-separated list is the same flag: --record-identity hash, path. The config key is record_identity, and the environment variable is SUPERSHELF_RECORD_IDENTITY. The default is path, which means path then hash. A bare hash means hash then path. A list does not expand, so [path] does not follow a rename.

A match rule can set its own list. Omitted, it inherits the profile default. The flag does not override a rule that set the key.

[[match_rules]]
name = "bill"
glob = "**"
record_identity = ["hash", "path"]

The two readings of one Bank2000 invoice are in Record.

items.title: See why it matched
items.text:
supershelf scan inspect prints how the match rules test kept files. It uses the same walk as scan files --quick: no hash, no mtime, and no ctime. The pattern order is in Matching.

The path argument is the same as List files. Omit it to print one line per kept file and no patterns. If any kept path equals the selector, every input traces that exact path only. Otherwise the selector traces each kept file whose path starts with it, with the same detail as a single file.

supershelf scan inspect
supershelf scan inspect "Bank2000/REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf"

Without a path, a hit looks like this:

match profile books input 1 Bank2000/REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf rule bank2000_statement kind invoice

A miss looks like this:

miss profile books input 1 notes/readme.txt

With a path, the default output prints each pattern that was actually tried, in rule and field order, and stops at the first hit:

profile books input 1 rule bank2000_statement filename_regex 'REL_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<receipt_id>\w{8})\.pdf' against 'REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf': hit
Matched rule bank2000_statement kind invoice for Bank2000/REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf in profile books input 1

A value that no kept file has stops the command. The same relative path in two inputs is traced twice. Each line includes the profile and the input index.

items.title: More detail
items.text:
-v also prints the path, directory, and filename, skipped fields, captured groups, and a line when an earlier rule won so later rules were not tried.

A skipped field has no patterns, or it is a directory field and the file sits in the input directory:

profile books input 1 rule bank2000_statement regex: skipped, no patterns

-vv also prints later patterns and later rules that matching never runs, marked not tried, with the candidate they would have used.

-vvv adds no extra inspect lines. Inspect writes these lines to stdout. The verbosity flags choose how many lines to print.

A bad pattern stops the command before the walk.

The next page stores values for a matched file: Set variables.

items.title: Set the document date
items.text:
__date__ is the document date. When it is set, the value is a calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. Supershelf uses that date for the document, including later output paths. This version does not write those paths. See Limits.

The commands used below are documented in Template commands.

Put the fallback list on default_vars, then let a rule try its own captured date first:

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[default_vars]
__date__ = [
  '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y%m%d") }}',
  '{{ pdf_cdate() }}',
  '{{ pdf_mdate() }}',
  '{{ file("ctime") }}',
]

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_statement"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = 'REL_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<receipt_id>\w{8})\.pdf'

[match_rules.vars]
__date__ = [
  '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y%m%d") }}',
  '{{ __date__ }}',
]
profile.books.yaml
default_vars:
  __date__:
    - '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y%m%d") }}'
    - '{{ pdf_cdate() }}'
    - '{{ pdf_mdate() }}'
    - '{{ file("ctime") }}'

match_rules:
  - name: bank2000_statement
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: 'REL_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<receipt_id>\w{8})\.pdf'
    vars:
      __date__:
        - '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y%m%d") }}'
        - '{{ __date__ }}'

regex_time_var reads the string already stored as date and returns YYYY-MM-DD. For REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf that is 2026-04-25. The rule list tries that first. {{ __date__ }} reads the string the earlier layer kept. It does not run the earlier candidate list again.

pdf_cdate() and pdf_mdate() read PDF info and also return YYYY-MM-DD. The file is opened only when a candidate calls one of them.

file("ctime") returns the stored UTC timestamp, such as 2026-04-25T16:28:00+00:00. That text is not YYYY-MM-DD, so the __date__ check fails this candidate. In the list above it is the last default_vars candidate, so that layer ends. On its own it does not become __date__. file("mtime") is the same kind of timestamp.

A __date__ candidate that renders to anything else fails, and the next candidate is tried. If every candidate in that layer misses, the earlier value stays. When no layer sets __date__, it is omitted and the command continues. The same rule applies to every other variable. The filename does not set __date__. mandatory: true stops the file when the value is still unset after the last layer.

__date__ is type date. vars_schema.__date__ may set desc, unit, mandatory, default, and validation. It cannot change the type. Quote date scalars in default_vars, rule vars, and kind files. An unquoted date is not a string, and those layers take a string or a list of strings.

The next page stores one path in a kind file: Set a value in the kind file.

items.title: Set variables
items.text:
supershelf scan vars prints one row per matched file. The vars cell lists the final values. How those values are layered is in Variables.

This profile sets a default owner, then replaces the vendor on the Bank2000 statement rule. The filename regex captures date and receipt_id. Those captures are facts. The rule can read them.

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"

[default_vars]
vendor = "UNKNOWN"
owner = "sample"

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_statement"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = 'REL_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<receipt_id>\w{8})\.pdf'

[match_rules.vars]
vendor = "Bank2000"
receipt = ["{{ receipt_id }}", "UNKNOWN"]

[[match_rules]]
name = "unsorted"
glob = "**"
profile.books.yaml
inputs:
  - path: inbox

default_vars:
  vendor: UNKNOWN
  owner: sample

match_rules:
  - name: bank2000_statement
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: 'REL_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<receipt_id>\w{8})\.pdf'
    vars:
      vendor: Bank2000
      receipt:
        - "{{ receipt_id }}"
        - UNKNOWN

  - name: unsorted
    glob: "**"

receipt tries {{ receipt_id }} first. If that name is missing, the next candidate, UNKNOWN, is kept. A candidate with no {{, {%, or {# is stored as written.

supershelf scan vars "Bank2000/REL_20260425_ab12cd34.pdf"

Example vars and sources cells. Internal facts are omitted unless --all is set. Names are alphabetical, and each sources line matches the name on that line.

vars                                      sources
date: 20260425                            fact
owner: sample                             default
receipt: ab12cd34                         rule:bank2000_statement
receipt_id: ab12cd34                      fact
vendor: Bank2000                          default, rule:bank2000_statement

vendor was set in default_vars and replaced by the rule, so both layers stay on its sources line. owner stays sample because the rule does not set it.

items.title: Declare a type
items.text:
vars_schema sets the type of a name. A filename group with that name is cast when the match stores it. The rules are in Variables.

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[vars_schema.amount]
type = "float"
unit = "EUR"

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_amount"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = 'REL_(?P<amount>[0-9]+[.][0-9]{2})\.pdf'
profile.books.yaml
vars_schema:
  amount:
    type: float
    unit: EUR

match_rules:
  - name: bank2000_amount
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: 'REL_(?P<amount>[0-9]+[.][0-9]{2})\.pdf'

For REL_12.50.pdf, the table shows amount: 12.50. In --format json and --format yaml that name is an object: value is 12.5, and value_sources lists the layers. display is not in the object. csv uses the same vars and sources cells as the table. Templates still read the string 12.50. EUR12.50 stops the file, because a regex group has no next candidate.

items.title: Print a JSON Schema
items.text:
supershelf schema prints those declared types. It does not scan the inbox and it does not write a kind file.

supershelf schema

The output is one JSON document, keyed by profile name. Add kind_schema when a kind should require a name or carry its own description:

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[kind_schema.invoice]
desc = "A vendor bill"

[kind_schema.invoice.vars_schema]
__date__ = ""
vendor = "vendor"

[kind_schema.invoice.vars_schema.amount]
schema = "amount"
mandatory = true
profile.books.yaml
kind_schema:
  invoice:
    desc: A vendor bill
    vars_schema:
      __date__:
      vendor: vendor
      amount:
        schema: amount
        mandatory: true

A string is the catalog name. Null or a blank string uses the local name. TOML has no null, so that form is "". An object may omit schema, which then uses the local name. invoice is then an object under $defs. amount is required. The rules are in Variables. A new CSV for that kind uses these local names as columns. An existing CSV gains any that are missing, on the right.

scan vars has no --quick. The walk always reads mtime, ctime, and sha256. The path argument is the same as List files. Omit it to list every matched file. If any kept path equals the selector, every input lists that exact path only. Otherwise the selector lists matched paths that start with it. A value that no kept file has stops the command. When a path is set, only the selected files are matched, so other files are not warned.

A key in one mapping cannot read a key that appears later in that same mapping. {{ vendor }} inside default_vars, next to vendor, still sees the previous layer, which is the fact scope. It does not see the candidate list being tried.

The next page turns the captured date into a calendar date: Set the document date.

items.title: Set a value in the kind file
items.text:
A kind file stores one row for a path. scan vars applies that row after the winning rule's vars. This is the last assignment layer. The cell replaces the value the rule stored. The lookup and the modes are in Kind files. The file shape is in Kind file.

For profile books and kind invoice, the first default path is profile.books.invoice.csv under the profile root.

Set the separator and the date format, then add a row for one statement:

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[config]
kind_overrides_sep = ";"
kind_overrides_date_format = "%d/%m/%Y"
profile.books.yaml
config:
  kind_overrides_sep: ";"
  kind_overrides_date_format: "%d/%m/%Y"
profile.books.invoice.csv
PATH;__date__;vendor;owner
banking_1/REL_20260425.pdf;25/04/2026;Bank2000;
Bank2000/card/CARD_1234_20211231.pdf;15/01/2026;;sample

vendor on the first row replaces the rule's vendor for that path only. The empty owner cell leaves the earlier owner in place. The text is stored as written. {{ owner }} would be those characters, not a template.

25/04/2026 is parsed with kind_overrides_date_format and stored as 2026-04-25. A cell that does not match that format stops the command. A blank __date__ cell leaves the earlier date in place.

supershelf scan vars

The default mode is auto. When the CSV already exists, invoice paths that are not in the file are appended. The new cells are empty, so this run still prints the values from the rule. Fill a cell and run the command again to use it.

kind_schema can name the variables for that kind and mark some of them mandatory. supershelf schema prints that shape. auto and always write those local names as CSV columns. Missing names are added on the right. Existing columns and cell text stay.

manual reads the file and does not append. always creates profile.books.invoice.csv when no candidate exists. disabled ignores kind files. --kind-overrides-mode sets the mode for this command. --dry-run reads and does not write. -v shows the dry-run message when a file would change.

The kind in the filename is the kind from the match rule.

The next page loads more than one profile: Use several profiles.
path: Set a value in the kind file

items.title: Use several profiles
items.text: Each profile file is a separate shelf. Profiles do not share scan results. Discovery rules are in Profiles.

items.title: Named files
items.text:
In the current directory, with no supershelf.toml, Supershelf loads every profile.NAME.toml, then .yaml, then .yml. One file per name. Names are sorted.

profile.books.toml
profile.cards.toml

The name comes from the filename. profile.books.toml is profile books. If config.profile inside that file is a different non-empty string, it is ignored and a warning is printed.

supershelf profiles
supershelf scan files

profiles lists both files. scan files walks each selected profile on its own. The profile column shows which file a row came from.

items.title: Choose a subset
items.text:
--profile is a comma-separated list. Spaces around names are ignored. The result keeps the requested order. A repeated name is kept once. An unknown name stops the command.

supershelf --profile cards,books profiles

SUPERSHELF_PROFILES is the same list. --profile wins when both are set.

SUPERSHELF_PROFILES=books supershelf scan kinds

With no selector, every discovered profile is kept.

items.title: One file for one profile
items.text:
If supershelf.toml, supershelf.yaml, or supershelf.yml exists in the directory, Supershelf loads only the first of those. It does not also load profile.NAME.* from that directory. The profile name is config.profile when that is set, otherwise default.

TOMLYAML supershelf.toml
[config]
profile = "books"

[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"
supershelf.yaml
config:
  profile: books

inputs:
  - path: inbox

--config points at a file or a directory and overrides SUPERSHELF_CONFIG. A missing explicit path does not fall through to the current directory.

The next page is a catalog of profiles for one inbox: Base.

items.title: Advanced
items.text: Same inbox as Base. These profiles set the document date, a value taken from the filename, and one kind-file row.

items.title: The inbox
items.text:
inbox/
  company/
    bank2000_account/
      REL_ACCTSTMT_100200300400_033123-ab12cd34.pdf
    bank2000_card/
      CARD_CREDCARD_1234_2023-11-15-ab12cd34.pdf
  home/
    northline/
      INV00000001_TR00000001_08292025.pdf
    metro_phone/
      2022-08-27 64.33.pdf
    civic_tax/
      Invoice 52.pdf
    signal_mobile/
      2025-05-18.pdf

The institution names are stand-ins: Bank2000, Northline Telecom, Metro Phone, Civic Tax, and Signal Mobile.

items.title: Document date
items.text:
__date__ is a calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. A rule that captures date parses that string with regex_time_var. The format is the one used in that filename. The commands are in Template commands.

Northline Telecom stores 08292025, read with %m%d%Y, which is 2025-08-29. The Bank2000 account statement stores 033123, read with %m%d%y, which is 2023-03-31. Bank2000 card, Metro Phone, and Signal Mobile already write YYYY-MM-DD. Civic Tax filenames have no date. default_vars tries the PDF creation date, then the PDF modification date.

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"
include = ["**/*.pdf"]

[default_vars]
__date__ = [
  '{{ pdf_cdate() }}',
  '{{ pdf_mdate() }}',
]

[[match_rules]]
name = "northline"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = 'INV\d+_TR\d+_(?P<date>\d{8})\.pdf'

[match_rules.vars]
__date__ = [
  '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%m%d%Y") }}',
  '{{ __date__ }}',
]

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_account"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = 'REL_ACCTSTMT_\d+_(?P<date>\d{6})-[0-9a-f]+\.pdf'

[match_rules.vars]
__date__ = [
  '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%m%d%y") }}',
  '{{ __date__ }}',
]

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_card"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = 'CARD_CREDCARD_\d+_(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})-[0-9a-f]+\.pdf'

[match_rules.vars]
__date__ = [
  '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y-%m-%d") }}',
  '{{ __date__ }}',
]

[[match_rules]]
name = "metro_phone"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = '(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) (?P<amount>\d+\.\d+)\.pdf'

[match_rules.vars]
__date__ = [
  '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y-%m-%d") }}',
  '{{ __date__ }}',
]

[[match_rules]]
name = "signal_mobile"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = '(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\.pdf'

[match_rules.vars]
__date__ = [
  '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y-%m-%d") }}',
  '{{ __date__ }}',
]

[[match_rules]]
name = "civic_tax"
kind = "invoice"
directory_glob = "home/civic_tax"
profile.books.yaml
inputs:
  - path: inbox
    include:
      - "**/*.pdf"

default_vars:
  __date__:
    - '{{ pdf_cdate() }}'
    - '{{ pdf_mdate() }}'

match_rules:
  - name: northline
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: 'INV\d+_TR\d+_(?P<date>\d{8})\.pdf'
    vars:
      __date__:
        - '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%m%d%Y") }}'
        - '{{ __date__ }}'

  - name: bank2000_account
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: 'REL_ACCTSTMT_\d+_(?P<date>\d{6})-[0-9a-f]+\.pdf'
    vars:
      __date__:
        - '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%m%d%y") }}'
        - '{{ __date__ }}'

  - name: bank2000_card
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: 'CARD_CREDCARD_\d+_(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})-[0-9a-f]+\.pdf'
    vars:
      __date__:
        - '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y-%m-%d") }}'
        - '{{ __date__ }}'

  - name: metro_phone
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: '(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) (?P<amount>\d+\.\d+)\.pdf'
    vars:
      __date__:
        - '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y-%m-%d") }}'
        - '{{ __date__ }}'

  - name: signal_mobile
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: '(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\.pdf'
    vars:
      __date__:
        - '{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y-%m-%d") }}'
        - '{{ __date__ }}'

  - name: civic_tax
    kind: invoice
    directory_glob: home/civic_tax

On a rule that captured date, the first candidate parses that group. {{ __date__ }} keeps the value default_vars already stored. Civic Tax has no capture, so its date comes from the PDF. A PDF with neither date leaves __date__ unset.

items.title: A value from the name
items.text:
Metro Phone captures amount. The rule stores that number and sets the vendor. amount is a float, and it must be zero or greater.

Northline Telecom is matched by its filename. The override sets __date__ on that one file. Quote it. The value is already YYYY-MM-DD.

inbox/
  home/
    northline/
      INV00000001_TR00000001_08292025.pdf
    metro_phone/
      2022-08-27 64.33.pdf
TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"
include = ["**/*.pdf"]

[vars_schema.amount]
type = "float"

[vars_schema.amount.validation]
ge = 0

[[match_rules]]
name = "northline"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = 'INV\d+_TR\d+_\d{8}\.pdf'

[[match_rules]]
name = "metro_phone"
kind = "invoice"
filename_regex = '(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) (?P<amount>\d+\.\d+)\.pdf'

[match_rules.vars]
vendor = "Metro Phone"
amount = ["{{ amount }}"]
profile.books.yaml
inputs:
  - path: inbox
    include:
      - "**/*.pdf"

vars_schema:
  amount:
    type: float
    validation:
      ge: 0

match_rules:
  - name: northline
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: 'INV\d+_TR\d+_\d{8}\.pdf'

  - name: metro_phone
    kind: invoice
    filename_regex: '(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) (?P<amount>\d+\.\d+)\.pdf'
    vars:
      vendor: Metro Phone
      amount:
        - "{{ amount }}"

{{ amount }} reads the group from the Metro Phone filename, 64.33.

items.title: A value stored for one path
items.text:
For profile books and kind invoice, the first default kind file is profile.books.invoice.csv under the profile root. This row sets the Bank2000 account statement. 31/03/2023 is read with kind_overrides_date_format and stored as 2023-03-31.

inbox/
  company/
    bank2000_account/
      REL_ACCTSTMT_100200300400_033123-ab12cd34.pdf
TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[config]
kind_overrides_sep = ";"
kind_overrides_date_format = "%d/%m/%Y"

[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"
include = ["**/*.pdf"]

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_account"
kind = "invoice"
directory_glob = "company/bank2000_account"
profile.books.yaml
config:
  kind_overrides_sep: ";"
  kind_overrides_date_format: "%d/%m/%Y"

inputs:
  - path: inbox
    include:
      - "**/*.pdf"

match_rules:
  - name: bank2000_account
    kind: invoice
    directory_glob: company/bank2000_account
profile.books.invoice.csv
PATH;__date__;vendor
company/bank2000_account/REL_ACCTSTMT_100200300400_033123-ab12cd34.pdf;31/03/2023;Bank2000

The default mode is auto. An invoice path that is missing from the file is appended. The modes are in Kind files.

The same mechanisms, without the walkthrough, are in Concepts.

items.title: Base
items.text:
These profiles classify one inbox. Copy the profile closest to your folders.

The institution names are stand-ins: Bank2000, Northline Telecom, Metro Phone, Civic Tax, and Signal Mobile.

items.title: The inbox
items.text:
inbox/
  company/
    bank2000_account/
      REL_ACCTSTMT_100200300400_033123-ab12cd34.pdf
    bank2000_card/
      CARD_CREDCARD_1234_2023-11-15-ab12cd34.pdf

      Invoice 52.pdf

inbox is the input. A path in a rule is relative to that directory. Rules run in list order. The first rule that matches wins. Matching rules are in Matching.

include keeps PDF files. Each profile below is complete.

items.title: One folder, one kind
items.text:
Signal Mobile and Civic Tax each have their own folder. One filename is only a date. The other has no shared pattern. directory_glob is that folder.

inbox/
  home/
    civic_tax/
      Invoice 52.pdf
    signal_mobile/
      2025-05-18.pdf
TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"
include = ["**/*.pdf"]

[[match_rules]]
name = "signal_mobile"
kind = "invoice"

[[match_rules]]
name = "civic_tax"

directory_glob = "home/civic_tax"

  - name: civic_tax

items.title: A specific folder, then a wider one
items.text:
The Bank2000 card folder and the Bank2000 account folder share the prefix company/bank2000_. The card rule is the exact directory. The account rule matches every remaining directory at that level.

inbox/
  company/
    bank2000_account/
      REL_ACCTSTMT_100200300400_033123-ab12cd34.pdf
    bank2000_card/
      CARD_CREDCARD_1234_2023-11-15-ab12cd34.pdf

[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"
include = ["**/*.pdf"]

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_card"
kind = "invoice"

[[match_rules]]
name = "bank2000_account"
kind = "invoice"

items.text:
Northline Telecom invoices look like INV00000001_TR00000001_08292025.pdf. Metro Phone bills look like 2022-08-27 64.33.pdf. filename_regex full-matches the filename, including .pdf. The folder is not part of the match.

match_rules:

profile.books.yaml

    include:

match_rules:

    kind: invoice

  - name: civic_tax

  - name: bank2000_card
