The next page reads dates and other values from these files: Advanced.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
Supershelf is a Python command. It needs Python 3.13 or newer. From a checkout of this repository:

pip install .

That installs the supershelf command. The version line is filled from the program:

supershelf 0.1.0

items.title: One profile
items.text:
Create profile.books.toml or profile.books.yaml in the directory where you will run the command. This example keeps every file under inbox and gives each one the kind unsorted.

TOMLYAML profile.books.toml
[[inputs]]
path = "inbox"

[[match_rules]]
name = "unsorted"
glob = "**"
profile.books.yaml
inputs:
  - path: inbox

match_rules:
  - name: unsorted
    glob: "**"

Put a file in inbox, then list what the profile loaded and what the walk kept:

supershelf profiles
supershelf scan files

profiles prints the profile name, the file type, and the config path. scan files prints each kept file. The path column is relative to inbox.

A file that no rule claims is still listed by scan files. scan kinds leaves it out and prints a warning. The catch-all rule above claims every kept file, so that warning does not appear.

items.title: Where to go next
items.text: List files adds include, exclude, and depth. Match a kind separates a Bank2000 statement from the rest. Set variables reads names out of the filename and can print them as JSON Schema.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
A command loads profiles, renders paths, walks inputs, matches rules, and resolves variables. The command line is the supported interface.

  1. ShelfConfigs finds config files, parses them, and applies --profile or SUPERSHELF_PROFILES. supershelf profiles stops after this step.
  2. ShelfProfile renders root_dir, database_file, and cache_file for one loaded file.
  3. InputScanner walks that profile's inputs and returns the kept files.
  4. Matcher compiles match_rules once and claims a kind for each kept file.

  5. VarPlan resolves facts, then default_vars, then the winning rule's vars, then the kind-file row for that path. The kind file is the last assignment layer. Each written name is cast to its vars_schema type. When that kind has a kind_schema entry, the names it lists use the overlaid spec. A name with no entry stays text. See Variables.

  6. record run compares that result with the profile database and appends events. record status prints the comparison and writes nothing.

scan files runs steps 1 to 3. scan kinds and scan inspect run steps 1 to 4. scan vars runs steps 1 to 5, and may create or append a kind file after the run succeeds. record status and record run run steps 1 to 6. record run does not create or append a kind file. schema loads the profile and prints JSON Schema. It does not walk inputs or write a kind file. scan vars and record run create the database file when meta() runs and the cache misses. --dry-run does not. scan files and scan kinds do not. scan inspect, schema, and profiles do not either. Nothing writes cache_file. There is no output tree.

Var modules are the extension point. A module listed in config.var_modules may export GLOBALS and FILTERS. Those callables are available inside variable templates. See Modules.

items.title: Command line
items.text:
Every command accepts --config, --profile, --dry-run, and --version, plus the log flags from the CLI library. The listings below are the program's own help text.

--config selects the config file or directory and overrides SUPERSHELF_CONFIG. --profile is a comma-separated list of profile names and overrides SUPERSHELF_PROFILES. --dry-run on scan vars reads kind files and does not create or append. On record run it prints the rows that would change and does not create the database. The other scan commands only print. See Limits.

The help text lists -vvvv. This program's log tiers stop at -vvv. -vvvv is rejected.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
A profile file is a mapping. TOML and YAML are accepted. .yml is YAML. Paths inside the file are described in Paths. Discovery is in Profiles.

Which file is loaded, and which profiles run:

  1. CLI: --config, --profile
  2. Environment: SUPERSHELF_CONFIG, SUPERSHELF_PROFILES
  3. Discovery in the current directory, then the user config directory
  4. Built-in defaults for omitted keys inside the file

There is no environment variable for root_dir or the other keys below, except kind_overrides_mode and record_identity. An omitted key uses its default. On the optional config keys, and on include, exclude, depth, and follow_symlinks, a YAML null is the same as omitting the key. An empty string and an empty list stay set. include: [] keeps no file. A candidate, and vars_schema.<name>.default, reject null: null is not unset. A command that reads a key stops if that key has the wrong type. supershelf profiles checks that the file is a mapping and that config.profile, when set, is a string. It does not render paths.

items.title: config
items.text:
These keys live under config.

Key Type Default Role profile string from the filename, or default Profile name when the filename is not profile.NAME.*. See Profiles. default_date_format string %Y-%m-%d strftime pattern for mtime and ctime in scan files. Not a template. root_dir string {{ __profile_dir__ }} Path template. Relative results resolve from the config directory. database_file string {{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.sqlite Path template. record run creates it when a row would change. scan vars and record run also create it when meta() runs and the cache misses. --dry-run does not. scan files and scan kinds do not. cache_file string {{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.cache Path template. Rendered, not created. record_identity string or list of strings path path, hash, or a list of those steps. A bare path means path then hash. A bare hash means hash then path. A list does not expand. "" and [] are invalid and do not fall back. See Record. var_modules list of strings none Importable modules. See Modules. kind_overrides_mode string auto auto, manual, always, or disabled. See Kind files. kind_overrides_date_format string default_date_format strptime format for a kind-file __date__ cell. kind_overrides_sep one character , CSV separator. YAML and TOML ignore it. See Kind file. kind_overrides_config list of strings the four default kind paths Path templates. First existing file wins. [] means no kind files. See Kind files.

Other keys under config are stored. This version does not interpret them.

items.title: Top level
items.text: Key Type Default Role inputs list of mappings required for a scan Folders to walk. See Inputs. match_rules list of mappings none First match wins. Missing means nothing matches. See Matching. default_vars mapping none Lowest assignment layer. See Variables. vars_schema mapping none Type of each variable name. A missing name is text. See Variables. kind_schema mapping none Per-kind names that point at vars_schema. See Variables.

items.title: inputs item
items.text:
Key Type Default path string required include list of strings omitted or null: keep every file the walk found. [] keeps no file exclude list of strings omitted or null: drop nothing. [] drops nothing depth integer 0 or greater 0, no recursion limit follow_symlinks boolean true

Unknown keys on an input stop the command.

items.title: match_rules item
items.text:
Key Type Role name string Rule name. Unique in the profile. kind string Kind stored for a hit. Defaults to name. regex string or list of strings Whole relative path. directory_regex string or list of strings Directory under the input. filename_regex string or list of strings Filename, including the extension. glob string or list of strings Whole relative path. directory_glob string or list of strings Directory under the input. filename_glob string or list of strings Filename. vars mapping Assignment layer for this rule. Ignored by matching. Read by scan vars. record_identity string or list of strings the profile default

A rule needs name or kind, and at least one pattern. Other unknown keys are ignored while matching.

items.title: vars_schema item
items.text:
Key Type Default desc string empty type text, int, float, bool, date, time, or datetime text unit string omitted mandatory boolean false default typed literal, string, or list of candidates omitted. Same slot as default_vars. validation mapping omitted

Unknown keys stop the command. default set here and in default_vars for the same name stops the command.

items.title: kind_schema item
items.text:
Key Type Default desc string empty vars_schema mapping required

Each vars_schema value is a catalog reference:

Value Meaning null or "" schema is the local name. YAML amount: is null. TOML has no null, so use amount = "". A blank string is the same. string That string is schema. my_amount: amount remaps the local name. mapping Keys below. Omitted, null, or blank schema uses the local name.

Each mapping:

Key Type Default schema string the local name. A vars_schema name, or __date__. desc string copied from the referenced spec unit string copied from the referenced spec mandatory boolean copied from the referenced spec. false loosens it for this kind. default typed literal, string, or list of candidates omitted. Not copied. Applies only to this kind's local name. validation mapping copied when omitted. A present mapping replaces the referenced one.

type and internal cannot be set here. Unknown keys stop the command. On a CSV, auto and always use these local names as columns. A kind that is not listed uses the declared vars_schema names. A name that is not a legal column is left out. With no schema columns, a new CSV still starts as PATH,__date__.

items.title: Variable values
items.text: In default_vars and rule vars, each value is a string or a list of strings. Quote scalars such as dates. An empty list stops the command. A kind-file cell is one string, not a list. After a candidate or a cell is accepted, it is cast to the name's type. A typed literal belongs on vars_schema.<name>.default. Details are in Variables and Kind file.

items.title: Environment
items.text: Variable Overrides Meaning SUPERSHELF_CONFIG --config wins File or directory. A blank or whitespace flag stops the command. A blank or whitespace variable is unset. A set value uses the same path rules as --config. SUPERSHELF_PROFILES --profile wins Comma-separated profile names. A blank flag stops the command. A blank or whitespace variable is unset, so every discovered profile is kept. SUPERSHELF_KIND_OVERRIDES_MODE --kind-overrides-mode wins auto, manual, always, or disabled. Wins over config.kind_overrides_mode.

items.title: Kind file
items.text:
A kind file is a list of rows for one kind. One row per path relative to the input. A missing variable is omitted. How the file is chosen is in Kind files.

A cell is one string. It is not a candidate list. It is not compiled, even when it contains {{, {%, or {#. An empty cell, a blank string, or a YAML or TOML null is absent. When the row is applied, a non-empty cell is cast to the name's type. text keeps surrounding spaces. The other types strip once. __date__ is parsed with kind_overrides_date_format and stored as YYYY-MM-DD.

Files are UTF-8. Invalid UTF-8 stops the command. A leading byte-order mark is accepted and is not part of the first column name. The suffix is .csv, .toml, .yaml, or .yml. .yml is the same text as YAML.

The examples below are the same two rows. The profile sets kind_overrides_sep to ; and kind_overrides_date_format to %d/%m/%Y. The stored dates are 2026-04-25 and 2026-01-15. An empty cell is absent. YAML and TOML ignore the separator.

CSVTOMLYAML profile.books.invoice.csv
PATH;__date__;vendor;owner
banking_1/REL_20260425.pdf;25/04/2026;Bank2000;
Bank2000/card/CARD_1234_20211231.pdf;15/01/2026;;sample
profile.books.invoice.toml
[[rows]]
path = "banking_1/REL_20260425.pdf"

[rows.vars]
vendor = "Bank2000"
__date__ = "25/04/2026"

[[rows]]
path = "Bank2000/card/CARD_1234_20211231.pdf"

[rows.vars]
__date__ = "15/01/2026"
owner = "sample"
profile.books.invoice.yaml
- path: banking_1/REL_20260425.pdf
  vars:
    vendor: Bank2000
    __date__: "25/04/2026"

- path: Bank2000/card/CARD_1234_20211231.pdf
  vars:
    __date__: "15/01/2026"
    owner: sample

items.title: CSV
items.text:
One data row per file. The header is checked by name and case. The first column is exactly PATH. __date__ is optional and may sit anywhere after PATH. Other columns are the user's, in the user's order.

config.kind_overrides_sep is the separator. Omitted, it is a comma. The file is not scanned to guess it. The separator must be one character. A value that is not a string, an empty string, or more than one character stops the command. A letter, a digit, _, whitespace, ", ', /, \, or a newline is rejected. Comma and semicolon are the expected values. | is allowed.

Read and append use that separator. A file written with another separator fails the header check. Cells that contain the separator, a double quote, or a newline are quoted with ".

The first column must be PATH. path or Path is an error. A missing PATH, or PATH in a later position, is an error. A header named SHA, sha, or Sha is an error: rows match on PATH. There is no DATE column. DATE, Date, and date are errors: the date column is __date__. A column that is not lowercase is an error. A duplicate column is an error.

A column other than PATH and __date__ must be lowercase and match [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*.

An empty file, or a file of whitespace only, is an empty table, not a missing-header error. A blank line is skipped. A row with values and an empty PATH is an error. A row with fewer cells than the header is padded with empty cells. A row with more cells than the header stops the command.

items.title: TOML and YAML
items.text:
YAML is a bare list. There is no key above it. Each item has path and vars. vars is a mapping of name to text. Omitted vars, or an empty mapping, adds no variables. Any other shape for vars stops the command. Unknown keys on the item are ignored.

TOML cannot be a root list, so the file is [[rows]] tables. Each table has path and a [rows.vars] table. The items are the same as YAML.

path is the path relative to the input, with / separators. It is an exact match, not a glob.

A name under vars must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. TOML rejects a duplicate key in one vars table. YAML keeps the last value for a duplicate key and does not stop. A missing path stops the command. A number, boolean, date, list, or nested mapping stops the command. Quote scalars such as dates. In YAML, also quote yes, no, on, and off, because those words become booleans.

items.title: Names
items.text:
A row must not set an internal name. __date__ is allowed. __kind__ is not.

Two rows with the same path: a warning, the first row is kept, and the later row stays in the file.

items.title: A new file
items.text:
A new file is an always create, or an auto or always replacement of an empty or whitespace-only file. manual does not write.

A new CSV header starts with PATH. When that kind has schema columns, those names follow in schema order, joined by kind_overrides_sep. A kind_schema entry supplies its local names. Otherwise the declared vars_schema names are used. Locked internals are left out. __date__ is included only when that schema lists it. A name that is not a legal column is left out. With no schema columns, the header is PATH and __date__. Omitted, that header is PATH,__date__. The semicolon example with no schema writes PATH;__date__. There is no SHA column and no DATE column. Then one row per matched file. Each new row sets PATH and leaves the other cells empty.

A new TOML or YAML file is the same rows, with path set and vars omitted.

auto and always append any missing schema columns to an existing CSV, on the right, in schema order. Columns already there stay, including names the schema does not list. Cell text is not rewritten. Each existing data row gains empty cells for the new columns. A short row is padded out to the old width first. A blank line stays blank. manual and disabled do not add columns. --dry-run logs the names and does not write. A real add is a debug log. An append then uses that header. PATH or path is filled. The other new cells are empty.

items.title: Templates
items.text: Supershelf has two template languages. Path settings use the small language. Variable values use Jinja when the string looks like a template.

items.title: Path templates
items.text:
Used by config.root_dir, config.database_file, config.cache_file, inputs.path, and each kind_overrides_config entry.

{{ __root_dir__ }}/profile.{{ __profile__ }}.sqlite
{{ __config_data__.config.profile }}
  • Replaces {{ name }} and {{ name.key }} once.
  • Spaces inside the braces are allowed.
  • The value must be a string. Nested keys walk mappings.
  • Text copied from the scope is not rendered again.
  • An unknown name, a missing key, or a non-string stops the command.
  • No filters, no function calls, and no {% blocks.

items.title: Variable templates
items.text:
Used by default_vars and rule vars. A kind-file cell is one literal string. It is not compiled, even when it contains {{.

A string with no {{, {%, or {# is a literal. It is stored as written.

Bank2000
{{ receipt_id }}
{{ regex_time_var(date, "%Y%m%d") }}
{{ account_tail(account) }}
  • Jinja, with strict undefined names and autoescape off.
  • The result must be a string.
  • An unknown name fails that candidate. The next candidate in the list can run.
  • A syntax error stops the command when the template is loaded.
  • Each distinct source is compiled once for that profile. Another profile in the same command compiles it again.
  • The rendered string is not rendered again.
  • A key cannot read a later key in the same mapping.
  • A reference to the key being rendered sees the previous layer.

Commands are listed in Template commands. Extra commands are in Modules.

items.title: Variable names
items.text:
Printed names come from the file, the winning regex, and the assignment layers. Profile names are available while a template renders and are not printed on their own. The layer order and the types are in Variables.

Built-in facts below are type text. __date__ is type date. A user name with no vars_schema entry is text.

items.title: Printed facts
items.text:
These are set from the file and the match. Assignments cannot replace them. __kind__ stays the kind from the match rule. scan vars prints them only with --all.

Name Value __kind__ Kind from the winning rule. __rule_name__ Winning rule name. __ctime__ Stored UTC ISO-8601 ctime. __mtime__ Stored UTC ISO-8601 mtime. __file_hash__ Lowercase sha256 of the file bytes. __file_name__ Filename. __file_stem__ Filename without the last suffix. archive.tar.gz is archive.tar. __file_ext__ Last suffix without the dot. archive.tar.gz is gz. Empty when there is no suffix. __file_path__ Path relative to the input, with / separators. __file_dir__ Directory relative to the input. Empty in the input directory.

Named regex groups are stored in pattern order and printed with the other names. The table sorts every name alphabetically. A group name that starts with __ stops the command before the walk. A group that reuses an internal name is dropped.

items.title: Document date
items.text:
Name Who may set it Value __date__ default_vars, rule vars, kind file Type date. Stored as YYYY-MM-DD.

__date__ is not an internal. The filename does not set it. In default_vars and rule vars, an empty string does not count as success. A candidate list that misses leaves an earlier value in place. A kind-file cell is parsed with kind_overrides_date_format and stored as YYYY-MM-DD. A blank cell is absent. A cell that does not match the format stops the command.

items.title: Profile scope
items.text:
These names are in scope for path templates and variable templates. They are not printed as their own rows. An assignment cannot reuse one of them. A name that starts with __ and is not a managed variable stops the command with "is not a supershelf variable". The managed names are the internal facts and __date__.

Name Value __profile__ Profile name. Alias of __profile_name__. __profile_name__ Profile name. __profile_type__ toml or yaml. __profile_path__ Absolute path of the config file. __profile_dir__ Directory of the config file. __profile_file__ Filename of the config file. __default_date_format__ config.default_date_format. __config_data__ The parsed config file. Dotted keys read nested mappings. __root_dir__ Rendered root directory. __database_file__ Rendered database path. record run creates it when a row would change. __cache_file__ Rendered cache path. The file is not created.

Kind-file path templates also see:

Name Value __kind__ The rule kind. __input__.path Absolute path of that input directory.

__kind__ and __input__.path are not in the general profile scope. An inputs path cannot read them.

items.title: Who may assign a name
items.text:
Name default_vars Rule vars Kind file __kind__ no no no other internals no no no __date__ yes yes yes a name that does not start with __ yes yes yes any other name that starts with __ no no no

A variable name matches [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*.
